incidente.resumo: Polish users could not type the letter Ś in Medium's editor: code added to suppress the browser save dialog blocked any Ctrl+S, and on Windows the Right Alt+S used to type Ś is mapped internally to Ctrl+Alt+S. The fix changed the code to block Ctrl+S only if the Alt key was not pressed.

descricao.texto: A user reported that, while writing an article in Polish, every letter could be typed except Ś, which did not appear when its key was pressed, and only on Medium.
trechos: A few weeks ago, someone reported this to us at Medium:
“I just started an article in Polish. I can type in every letter, except Ś. When I press the key for Ś, the letter just doesn’t appear. It only happens on Medium.”

descricao.texto: Medium's editor code intercepted S pressed with Command (metaKey) or Ctrl to trigger a save and prevent the default action (the browser save dialog). In Poland, Ś is typed with Right Alt+S, and Windows maps Right Alt internally to Ctrl+Alt, so Right Alt+S appeared as Ctrl+Alt+S and was blocked, making Ś impossible to type.
trechos: It translates to: if S happens to be pressed with Command (*metaKey,* used by Macintoshes) or Ctrl (used by Windows or Linux PCs), first: prompt our editor to save what it’s doing (even though we’d autosave it soon anyway), and second: prevent anything else that would normally happen… in this case the annoying browser save dialog.
1. Through historical circumstance, people in Poland use Right Alt+S to type in Ś.
Right Alt in Windows was internally mapped as a rarely-used combination of Ctrl and Alt pressed together.
2. Because of an obscure technical decision, Right Alt+S is mapped internally to Ctrl+Alt+S.

4. Medium was overriding whatever default action happened when you pressed Ctrl+S, thinking it’s just a browser save dialog it was canceling… and never realizing it could be something else: *a letter Ś.*
And so, typing Ś became impossible.

descricao.texto: Code added to the Medium editor to suppress the browser save dialog: on S pressed with Command (metaKey) or Ctrl, save and prevent the default action, without checking whether Alt was pressed.
trechos: However, at some point we added a little bit of code to our editor to make the save dialog go away:

It translates to: if S happens to be pressed with Command (*metaKey,* used by Macintoshes) or Ctrl (used by Windows or Linux PCs), first: prompt our editor to save what it’s doing (even though we’d autosave it soon anyway), and second: prevent anything else that would normally happen… in this case the annoying browser save dialog.

passos.texto: The editor code was patched to block Ctrl+S only if the Alt key was not pressed; the fix was made the week before the article.
trechos: Instead of blindly blocking Ctrl+S, we could block Ctrl+S *only if Alt key was not pressed.*
We fixed this last week, and it wasn’t a lot of work.

observacoes: The article is a narrative by a Medium engineer; the report came "a few weeks ago" and the fix "last week", with no dates in the extracted text. The page ends with a call for ambassadors (recruiting footer). The conditional in Medium's codebase is now copiously commented so that people coming later understand it; the text gives this as documentation, not as a measure against recurrence.
